I've been working this land for over forty years. I know what grows here in Quzhou and what the well can handle. My two sons work in the city now, so it is mostly me and my wife doing the farm work, with help during busy seasons. I need to keep things manageable while still bringing in decent income.

**My thinking:**

The wheat-maize rotation on the main plot is the backbone. I do not change that. Wheat goes in October on about 4 mu, then maize follows on the same ground right after June harvest — no-tillage after wheat because the soil is already worked and I save time when I'm busy with other things. For wheat I use the improved Jimai variety that most neighbors here use. For maize I always use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or similar, the cooperative sells it and yields are reliable. I apply basal fertilizer before wheat and topdress at jointing. Maize gets one basal application and one topdress at big bell stage.

The chili is my cash crop on the remaining 2.5 mu. It demands the most labor and the most water, but the price is good. I transplant seedlings in late April. Chili needs more irrigation than the grain crops and I spray fungicide and insecticide more often because blight and aphids come every year without fail. I use improved commercial variety — I bought seed from the market last year and it did well.

I irrigate wheat three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Maize I irrigate at planting and then at silking if it is dry. Chili I irrigate more frequently through the summer.

I do not push yield beyond what the land and water can support. I have done this long enough to know that overloading on nitrogen brings problems — lodging in wheat, and the maize gets tall but hollow.
